# 1) Setup

```{r Setup, message=FALSE}

#install.packages("nasapower") #
#install.packages("beepr")

library(janitor) # to clean data
library(dplyr) # wranglingdd
library(tidyr) # wrangling
library(readr) # to export csv
library(nasapower) # for NASA POWER API
library(purrr) # for mapping
library(beepr) # for beep
```

```{r create a function}
get_weather <- function(lon, lat, yr, site_name ) {
  cat("Running:", site_name, yr, "\n")
  x <- get_power(
    community = "AG",
    lonlat = c(lon, lat),
    dates = c(paste0(yr, "-01-01"), paste0(yr, "-12-31")),
    pars = c(
      "T2M",
      "T2M_MAX",
      "T2M_MIN",
      "PRECTOTCORR",
      "ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN"
    ),
    temporal_api = "daily"
  )
  
  Sys.sleep(1)  # avoid be banned by api limit 
   return(x) # return weather data frame
}


```

```{r test func}
weather_test_func <- meta_unique %>% slice(1:5) %>%

    weather = pmap(
      list(longitude, latitude, year, site),
      ~ get_weather(..1, ..2, ..3, ..4)
    )
  ) %>%
  tidyr::unnest(weather)
```

# 3) Data wrangling

## a. On training data

```{r clean_names }
meta_cleaned <- clean_names(Meta)
soil_cleaned <- clean_names(Soil)
trait_cleaned <- clean_names(Trait)

glimpse(soil_cleaned)

```

Trying to merge three csv. But lots of problems on site-year. So we have to deal with it before merge. Different code plus num(e.g TXH1, TXH2), means they are different site, means different lan and lon.

later suffix either lower case a/b or late/early(e.g "MOH1a", "MOH1-rep2") means different rep/block info, but doesn't affect the lan and lon info.

```{r handling site-year}
# clean soil, separate site-year
soil_separate <- soil_cleaned %>%
  # "_(?=[^_]+$)" means look for the last "_" from right side to do the separation.
  separate(site, into = c("site", "year"), sep = "_(?=[^_]+$)") %>%
  mutate(year = as.integer(year))


# trait,soil, and meta all have different site-year. check the number
trait_key <- trait_cleaned %>%
  distinct(site, year)
# 270 rows

meta_key <- meta_cleaned %>%
  distinct(site, year)
# 251 rows

soil_key <- soil_separate %>%
  distinct(site, year)
# 186 keys


# avoid many-to-many merge
## check meta lat,lon base on site-year info
meta_cleaned %>%
  count(site, year) %>%
  filter(n > 1)

meta_check_site_year<-meta_cleaned %>%
  group_by(site, year) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            n_distinct_lat = n_distinct(latitude),
            n_distinct_lon = n_distinct(longitude))
## lan and lon all same, so we can use distinct as long as they're are from same site code, even if the lan and lon differ slightly. But we have to choose one set of lan and lon from the same site code, to avoid the many-to-many merge problem.

# average the lon and lat for the same site code
meta_unique <- meta_cleaned %>%
  group_by(site, year) %>%
  summarise(
    latitude = mean(latitude, na.rm = TRUE),
    longitude = mean(longitude, na.rm = TRUE),
    previous_crop = first(previous_crop),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


# do the same to soil data
soil_unique <- soil_separate %>%
  group_by(site, year) %>%
  summarise(
    soilp_h = mean(soilp_h, na.rm = TRUE),
    om_pct = mean(om_pct, na.rm = TRUE),
    soilk_ppm = mean(soilk_ppm, na.rm = TRUE),
    soilp_ppm = mean(soilp_ppm, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# now we have the soil and meta data with distinct site year so that we can avoid that many-to-many problem when merge to trait data 

# set same site for 3 csv

# test regular expression
sub("^([A-Za-z]+[0-9]+).*", "\\1",
    c("TXH1-Late", "MOH1a", "MOH1-rep2", "IAH1"))
#  "TXH1" "MOH1" "MOH1" "IAH1"

trait2 <- trait_cleaned %>%
  rename(detailed_site = site) %>%
  mutate(
    site = detailed_site %>%
    sub("^([A-Za-z]+[0-9]+).*", "\\1", x = .) # remove a/b/c,rep, later/early
      
  ) %>% 
  # move to 3rd col
  relocate(site, .after = detailed_site)

# check trait2, row #943, IAH1a -> IAH1, it worked.
# row # 49901 2017 TXH1-Early -> TXH1, it worked.

```

Now, we make the site clearly separate from detailed site in trait data. And we make site unique in meta and soil data. We can start merge.

```{r  merge data & check }

# merge
data_merged <- trait2 %>%
  left_join(meta_unique, by = c("site" = "site", "year" = "year")) %>%
  left_join(soil_unique, by = c("site" = "site", "year" = "year"))

# check many-to-many problem
nrow(trait2) == nrow(data_merged)
# True means we did it right, there's no many-to-many problem happened.


# overwrite with rep info in soil data
soil_rep <- soil_separate %>%
  mutate(
    site_base = str_remove(site, "_\\d+$"),
    rep_soil = as.integer(str_extract(site, "(?<=_)\\d+$"))
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(rep_soil)) %>%
  select(site_base, year, rep_soil, soilp_h, om_pct, soilk_ppm, soilp_ppm)

data_fix <- data_merged %>%
  left_join(
    soil_rep,
    by = c("site" = "site_base", "year" = "year", "replicate" = "rep_soil"),
    suffix = c("", "_rep")
  )

data_fix <- data_fix %>%
  mutate(
    soilp_h = coalesce(soilp_h_rep, soilp_h),
    om_pct = coalesce(om_pct_rep, om_pct),
    soilk_ppm = coalesce(soilk_ppm_rep, soilk_ppm),
    soilp_ppm = coalesce(soilp_ppm_rep, soilp_ppm)
  ) %>%
  select(-ends_with("_rep"))
# read the row#63403 &63404, the soil is different now. Means we give the different rep to trait data.

# save as merged data
write_csv(data_fix, "../data/training/training_merged.csv")
```



This means we merge correctly, even though we lack some site-year info initially from meta and soil data.

Then we can do some data wrangling & feature engineering on weather data.

```{r separate year and site for soil and meta}
# get unique site year, by average
```


# 4) Feature engineering on weather data

## a. Download weather data again

Based on updated view on the merged trait data, we have to download weather again for all the unique site-year across whole 2013-2024 12 years.

```{r read the data,check the site-year match }
#check the distint site-year of weather
weather <- read.csv("../data/weather_raw.csv")
weather_unique_siteyear <- weather %>%

# 251 rows

# 39 rows,

  group_by(site) %>%
  summarise(
    latitude = mean(latitude, na.rm = TRUE),
    longitude = mean(longitude, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"

```

```{r create a function}
get_weather <- function(lon, lat, site_name) {
  cat("Running:", site_name, "\n")
  
  x <- get_power(
    community = "AG",
    lonlat = c(lon, lat),
    dates = c("2013-01-01", "2024-12-31"),
    pars = c(
      "T2M",
      "T2M_MAX",
      "T2M_MIN",
      "PRECTOTCORR",
      "ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN"
    ),
    temporal_api = "daily"
  )
  
  x$site <- site_name
  
  Sys.sleep(0.5)
  
  return(x)
}


```

## c. EDA for weather
Let's create some density plots to explore the weather data distributions.

```{r EDA for weather data}

weather2 <- weather %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = T2M:ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = value)) + 
  geom_density() +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free") 
weather2
```

On weather data, we have radiation, precipitation, temp mean, min and max. And we have the plant and harvest date on training data. There are **two components** that we can consider when feature engineering weather data:\
1. Summarizing time **window size**\
- Weekly ✅ - Monthly\
- Every 2 months\
- Growing season ✅ - Based on crop growth stages ✅

2.  Summarizing **function**\

-   Mean ✅
-   Sum ✅
-   Standard deviation

Before we decide, let's check the plant and harvest date.

```{r check plant and harvest date}
train_data <- read_csv("../data/training/training_merged.csv")

train_data2 <- train_data %>%
  mutate(
    date_planted = as.Date(date_planted, format = "%m/%d/%y"),
    date_harvested = as.Date(date_harvested, format = "%m/%d/%y"),
    season_length = as.numeric(date_harvested - date_planted)
  )

train_data2

```

Notice every site-year plant/harvest at different date, and the period of growth also different. So we decide to use relative growth period as the time scale for feature engineering on weather data. So we can set **10 quantile stages** for corn.

Get these values for every stage: **GDD** , Growing Degree Days: GDD = ((Tmax + Tmin) / 2) - Tbase For corn, let's set: Tbase = 10°C Tmax cap = 30°C Tmin floor = 10°C

**sum of radiation**

**sum of precipitation**

**mean of T2M/max/min**

```{r  phenology info}
# phenology data frame
pheno_date <- train_data2 %>%
  group_by(site, year) %>%
  summarise(
    date_planted = date_planted,
    date_harvested = date_harvested ,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

 pheno_date %>%
  count(site, year, date_planted, date_harvested) %>%
  arrange(site, year)
# check the result to find out that in same site-year, harvest date might slightly changed 1-3days. This change is from rep and block difference, since this info is not provided in test data, so we decide to ignore it.
 
# we choose the max dates for same site year, reason is harvest may last for couples of days.  
 pheno_date2 <- pheno_date %>%
  group_by(site, year) %>%
  summarise(
    date_planted = first(date_planted),
    date_harvested = max(date_harvested, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
# 264 rows

  

```

```{r filter out the doy of growth period in weather data}
weather3 <- weather %>% 
  clean_names() %>%
  left_join(pheno_date2, by = c("site", "year")) %>%
  filter(yyyymmdd >= date_planted & yyyymmdd <= date_harvested)
# weather3: one row for one day, and start from plant date finish at harvest date for each site-year.
weather3 %>%
  distinct(site, year) %>%
  nrow()
# 262 rows, means 2 rows of site-year missing.
anti_join(
  pheno_date2 %>% distinct(site, year),
  weather3 %>% distinct(site, year),
  by = c("site", "year")
)
# These two site-year do not have correct lat and lon info: NYH1 in 2015, TXH4 in 2019.
```

```{r divide into 10 staged based on quantile}
# calculate the stage progress
weather3 <- weather3 %>%
  mutate(
    season_length = as.numeric(date_harvested - date_planted),
    dap = as.numeric(yyyymmdd - date_planted),
    # dap:days after planting
    progress = dap / season_length
  )

# create 10 stages
weather3 <- weather3 %>%
  mutate(
    stage = cut(
      progress,
      breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1),
      include.lowest = TRUE,
      labels = paste0("s", 1:10)
    )
  )



```

```{r save weather stage}
write_csv(weather3,
          "../data/weather_stage.csv")
```


Finally we can calculate the GDD now based on the growing stage. **GDD** , Growing Degree Days: GDD = ((Tmax + Tmin) / 2) - Tbase

```{r calculate the GDD}
# the reason of this is, corn is not growing under 10 degree, only growing from 10-30, not growing over 30 degree.
weather4 <- weather3 %>%
  mutate(
    tmax_adj = pmin(t2m_max, 30),
    tmin_adj = pmax(t2m_min, 10),
    gdd = pmax(((tmax_adj + tmin_adj) / 2) - 10, 0)
  )

```

```{r get weather feature based on stage}
# group by stage
weather_stage <- weather4 %>%
  group_by(site, year, stage) %>%
  summarise(
    gdd = sum(gdd, na.rm = TRUE),
    prcp = sum(prectotcorr, na.rm = TRUE),
    rad  = sum(allsky_sfc_sw_dwn, na.rm = TRUE),
    t2m  = mean(t2m, na.rm = TRUE),
    t2max = max(t2m_max, na.rm =TRUE),
    t2min = min(t2m_min, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```


```{r weathre feature wide}
weather_stage_wide <- weather_stage %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = stage,
    values_from = c(gdd, prcp, rad, t2m, t2max, t2min),
    values_fill = 0
  )
# still the 262 rows, means the number of unique site-year, same rows
```



## d. Feature refinement
Now we have stage wide weather data, but we could do more like get the sum of gdd across whole growth period, which means the sum of 10 stages.
```{r feature refinement }
weather_stage_wide2 <- weather_stage_wide %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    # add total gdd, percipitation, radiation across 10 stages.
    total_gdd  = sum(c_across(gdd_s1:gdd_s10), na.rm = TRUE),
    total_prcp = sum(c_across(prcp_s1:prcp_s10), na.rm = TRUE),
    total_rad  = sum(c_across(rad_s1:rad_s10), na.rm = TRUE),
    # add tem mean, max, min across 10 stages.
    avg_t2m    = mean(c_across(t2m_s1:t2m_s10), na.rm = TRUE),

    max_t2max  = max(c_across(t2max_s1:t2max_s10), na.rm = TRUE),
    min_t2min  = min(c_across(t2min_s1:t2min_s10), na.rm = TRUE),
    
    # do more stages sparation like 3 stages: early, mid and late.
    # here is gdd
    gdd_early  = sum(c_across(gdd_s1:gdd_s3), na.rm = TRUE),
    gdd_mid    = sum(c_across(gdd_s4:gdd_s7), na.rm = TRUE),
    gdd_late   = sum(c_across(gdd_s8:gdd_s10), na.rm = TRUE),
    # do prcp also
    prcp_early = sum(c_across(prcp_s1:prcp_s3), na.rm = TRUE),
    prcp_mid   = sum(c_across(prcp_s4:prcp_s7), na.rm = TRUE),
    prcp_late  = sum(c_across(prcp_s8:prcp_s10), na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

```

```{r  more weather feature plans}
# We ignore the sum of radiation of 3 stages last chunk. Because it might now as important as the prcp and gdd. We can put this into another file, and see the result difference when training model.
weather_stage_wide3 <- weather_stage_wide %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    # add total gdd, percipitation, radiation across 10 stages.
    total_gdd  = sum(c_across(gdd_s1:gdd_s10), na.rm = TRUE),
    total_prcp = sum(c_across(prcp_s1:prcp_s10), na.rm = TRUE),
    total_rad  = sum(c_across(rad_s1:rad_s10), na.rm = TRUE),
    # add tem mean, max, min across 10 stages.
    avg_t2m    = mean(c_across(t2m_s1:t2m_s10), na.rm = TRUE),

    max_t2max  = max(c_across(t2max_s1:t2max_s10), na.rm = TRUE),
    min_t2min  = min(c_across(t2min_s1:t2min_s10), na.rm = TRUE),
    
    # do more stages sparation like 3 stages: early, mid and late.
    # here is gdd
    gdd_early  = sum(c_across(gdd_s1:gdd_s3), na.rm = TRUE),
    gdd_mid    = sum(c_across(gdd_s4:gdd_s7), na.rm = TRUE),
    gdd_late   = sum(c_across(gdd_s8:gdd_s10), na.rm = TRUE),
    # do prcp also
    prcp_early = sum(c_across(prcp_s1:prcp_s3), na.rm = TRUE),
    prcp_mid   = sum(c_across(prcp_s4:prcp_s7), na.rm = TRUE),
    prcp_late  = sum(c_across(prcp_s8:prcp_s10), na.rm = TRUE),
    # do rad also
    rad_early = sum(c_across(rad_s1:rad_s3), na.rm = TRUE),
    rad_mid   = sum(c_across(rad_s4:rad_s7), na.rm = TRUE),
    rad_late  = sum(c_across(rad_s8:rad_s10), na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

```


```{r Exporting weather wide}
write_csv(weather_stage_wide2,
          "../data/weather_stage_wide.csv")
```

```{r Exporting weather wide-plan2}
write_csv(weather_stage_wide3,
          "../data/weather_stage_wide_plan2.csv")
```

Now we have merged train data, merged test data, and weather wide data.


# 5) Final check before train model
We can start train model at this stage, but we may check the data so that we can decide the further direction. or whether we need to do more data wrangling about the current dataset.

## a. Check all 3 csv files
```{r check 3 csv files}
train_mer <- read_csv("../data/training/training_merged.csv")
test_mer <- read_csv("../data/testing/testing_merged.csv")
weather_stage_wide <- read_csv("../data/weather_stage_wide.csv")

colnames(train_mer)
colnames(test_mer)
colnames(weather_stage_wide)

setdiff(names(train_mer), names(test_mer))
# so we don't have these cols in test data
#"detailed_site"  "replicate"      "block"          "date_planted"  
#[5] "date_harvested" "grain_moisture"

setdiff(names(test_mer), names(train_mer))

 
```
```{r select cols for train and test data}
train_mer2 <- train_mer %>%
  dplyr::select(-detailed_site, -replicate, -block,-date_planted,-date_harvested,-grain_moisture)
# we do the GDD and stage stuff, so let's remove plant and harvest date.
# rep and block not in the test, only depend on site name, remove.
# what about moisture, it's also predicted values of corn grain, not in the soil. remove.

setdiff(names(train_mer2), names(test_mer)) 
# no col difference now. Finally!
```
```{r check NA data}
colMeans(is.na(train_mer2))
colMeans(is.na(test_mer))
```
## b. Conclusion before training
Because the soil missing NA is bit higher (around 30%), we may consider just remove these col to see how it affect the prediction. We can try keep them at first place. So now we have 2 different train features(cols) before we train.
Plan 1: weather_stage_wide. That means we have everything but sum of radiation.
Plan 2: weather_stage_wide2, add radiation cols.
Plan 3: remove all soil cols.
Let's try from the plan 1.

```{r move weather to train and test data}
train_final <- train_mer2 %>%
  left_join(weather_stage_wide, by = c("site", "year"))
# no more rows, 83 cols, means good!


test_final <- test_mer %>%
  left_join(weather_stage_wide, by = c("site", "year"))
# same, 83 cols, means good!

# let's save 
write_csv(train_final,
          "../data/training/train_final.csv")
saveRDS(train_final, "../data/training/train_final.rds")

write_csv(test_final,
          "../data/testing/test_final.csv")

# to read rds file.
train_final2 <- readRDS("../data/training/train_final.rds")
# checked, it's compressed into rds file to reduce the size of train file.

```
